Marissa, thanks for the summary, that captures it well. A couple clarifications from our side after chatting with Security: 

- RBAC: we need role separation between platform admins, support engineers, and auditor roles. Support should have ephemeral access scoped to the tenant and time-limited.
- Break-glass: must be fully auditable. We prefer a ticket + manager approval flow but need the option for emergency one-click escalation with mandatory post-incident justification logged.
- Logs & retention: access logs (who/which token, IP, actions) should be retained for 90 days by default; audit records for privileged actions should be retained for 2 years.
- PII handling: any fields marked PII should be redacted in standard support views; full unredacted logs must be stored encrypted and only retrievable under break-glass with approval.
- Data residency: us-east-1 requirement remains.
- KMS: we prefer BYOK and a KMS integration where customer key access revocation can disable decryption of stored content.

Two asks: can you confirm Redwood's support access approval logging (store of approvals, approver identity, timestamp, justification) and whether you surface exportable audit reports? Also share any SOC2 or security whitepaper you have.

If you can get the RBAC doc + sample audit report, we can review internally and move to a MAP sign-off.


Jordan
Jordan Miles
Head of Infrastructure, FinTrust

Jordan / Priya,

Appreciate the detailed notes - yes, we can support all of those requirements. Quick answers and where to find the artifacts: 

Support access / break-glass
- Redwood provides an auditable break-glass flow: support opens a request, your on-call manager approves (or an emergency one-click escalation is available). Every break-glass action records approver identity, timestamp, justification, and the specific data objects accessed.
- All break-glass events are retained in the audit log and can be exported as CSV/JSON for compliance reviews.

RBAC
- Tenant-scoped roles, least-privilege templates (support, developer, ops, auditor).
- Role elevation is time-limited and bound to sessions; elevations expire automatically.

Logging & retention
- Access logs: default 90-day retention; privileged-action audit events stored for 2 years (configurable per-contract).
- PII redaction: support UI masks configurable fields; unredacted logs are encrypted and only retrievable under a break-glass event.

KMS / encryption
- BYOK supported via AWS KMS; customer key rotation and revocation are supported. If a key is revoked, data-at-rest becomes unreadable until a new key is provided.

Attachments & next steps
- Attached: redwood_rbac_overview.pdf (RBAC diagrams and role mappings) and fintrust_mutual-action-plan.xlsx (MAP with proposed milestones + tentative dates).
- Dev (cc'd) will run a technical deep-dive showing the support workflow and an exportable audit report sample.
- Can we schedule 45 mins on Tue 2026-12-08 or Wed 2026-12-09? We proposed slots in the MAP, please pick one.

I'll also drop our SOC2 summary and a sample audit report link to the HubSpot record.
